name: Banbasa–Nepal Border Highway
facts: Runs from NH 9 at Banbasa a few kilometres to the Nepal border.
Bhimdatta, on the Nepalese side, is also known as Mahendranagar.
It is one of the main road crossings into far-western Nepal.
The Sharda river, called the Mahakali in Nepal, forms much of the India–Nepal boundary in this area.
It was made a national highway in July 2020, officially running from NH 9 near the Jagbuda bridge to border pillar 802/11.
significance: A short national highway link from NH 9 at Banbasa, in Uttarakhand's Champawat district, to the Nepal border a few kilometres east of the town, across from Bhimdatta (Mahendranagar). It is one of the crossings between the Kumaon foothills and far-western Nepal, and it carries the cross-border trade and traffic of that corner of the frontier.

relatedRoads.label: Met at Banbasa, where this road begins

travelNotes: A short road, but the border crossing at the end has customs and immigration formalities — allow time for them.
futureUpgrades: NHAI is building a new four-lane link from NH 9 near the Jagbuda bridge in Banbasa to the Nepal border at Dodhara Chandani, where Nepal plans a dry port.
